kill_fact: Both legs fail: the event is spent, and the floor the sizing rests on does not exist. (1) CATALYST FIRED, VERIFIED. FDA granted FULL (not accelerated) approval of REVTORPYK (gedatolisib) with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, on 14 July 2026, three days ahead of the 17 July 2026 PDUFA goal date disclosed in the 20 January 2026 acceptance release -- confirmed on FDA's own approved-drugs page. The single binary this seat was underwritten for resolved FAVOURABLY and the equity fell anyway: $111.05 on 14 July (announced 16:53 ET, after the close) to $91.51 on 15 July (-17.6%), $82.27 on 27 July, against a 52-week high of $151.02, and below both the 50-day ($105.30) and 200-day ($102.82) averages. The spread did not merely close, it inverted. Nothing dated and binding replaces it: the sNDA for the PIK3CA-mutant population is a company SUBMISSION guided to a quarter (any ruling lands ~mid-2027), and 'late Q3 2026' launch is company guidance that has already moved once. (2) THE FLOOR BREAKS -- AND HARDER THAN THE DOSSIER ADMITS, because the balance sheet in the dossier is wrong. Celcuity issued $575M of 0.250% converts due 1 August 2032, not $500M: the $75M over-allotment was exercised IN FULL on 4 June 2026 and the issuance completed 8 June 2026, for net proceeds of ~$557.0M, not the ~$484.3M pre-greenshoe estimate the thesis carries. More seriously, the dossier omits an entire second tranche of debt: $201,250,000 of 2.750% convertible senior notes DUE 1 AUGUST 2031, issued 1 August 2025 and never repurchased -- the June 2026 proceeds funded only the ~$137.5M Oxford Finance repayment. Total convertible principal is therefore ~$776M, not $500M, and the repeated claims 'nothing to repay before 2032' and 'no maturity before 2032' are FALSE. Rolling $387.1M of cash and short-term investments at 31 March 2026 forward through ~$52M/qtr burn, +$557.0M net proceeds and -$137.5M Oxford gives roughly $750M of cash against ~$776M of converts: net cash is approximately ZERO to slightly NEGATIVE, not the '+$140M, roughly $3 a share' that both the bear case and the moderator lean on as 'the only hard number underneath.' So the true structure is a fired catalyst, no contractual backstop of any kind (no acquirer under contract, no CVR, no recovery value), and a balance sheet contributing ~$0/share. The $55 downside_floor and the board's $60 floor are both modelled peak-sales valuations that already assume the launch broadly works; beneath them nothing catches the price. A single-product, single-indication, pre-revenue commercial-launch bet with an unbounded left tail does not belong in a defined-risk event sleeve. One point AGAINST the bear for fairness: the tolerability kill is somewhat overstated -- FDA's label states stomatitis mitigation measures were generally effective, with most patients resolving to a lower grade within 2 weeks.
corrections: MATERIAL -- three linked balance-sheet errors that together delete the claimed floor. (1) The June 2026 convertible is $575,000,000 principal, not $500,000,000: the $75M over-allotment was exercised in full on 4 June 2026, issuance completed 8 June 2026, net proceeds ~$557.0M (the ~$484.3M in the dossier is the pre-greenshoe estimate). (2) The dossier omits $201,250,000 of 2.750% convertible senior notes DUE 1 AUGUST 2031 ($175M plus a $26.25M over-allotment, issued 1 August 2025), still outstanding -- the June 2026 use of proceeds repaid only the Oxford Finance term loan (~$137.5M) and does not touch them. Total convertible principal is ~$776M and the FIRST maturity is 2031, so 'nothing to repay before 2032' is false. NOTE the composition: the $195.6M of long-term debt on the 31 March 2026 balance sheet is the 2031 converts at amortised cost, and the $127.9M in other non-current liabilities is the Oxford term loan -- a prior skeptic pass mis-assigned BOTH to Oxford and so reached the right net-cash answer by the wrong route. (3) Net cash is therefore approximately ZERO (roughly $750M cash vs ~$776M converts), NOT '+$140M / ~$3 a share'. Every SoP line that adds ~$640M of cash and subtracts $500M of debt is overstated by roughly $165M, about $3.2/share across the bull ($130-177), base ($110) and bear ($50-58) cases. That is immaterial to the valuation RANKING but fatal to the 'defined risk' claim, which is the only reason this name sits in this book. MINOR: (a) 'The decision was fully priced at $151.02' conflates the 52-week high with the pre-decision price -- CELC closed $103.79 on 13 July and $111.05 on 14 July 2026 before the -$19.54 / -17.6% session on 15 July; the -46%-from-high and -17.6% figures themselves are correct. (b) The 2032 notes convert at ~$124.53/share (8.0302 shares per $1,000; a ~40% premium to the 3 June 2026 close), i.e. ~51% out of the money at $82.27 -- deferred dilution, and the notes rank ahead of shareholders until then. (c) CONFIRMED AS CARRIED: live price $82.27 (27 July 2026 close), 52wk high $151.02, 50d $105.30, 200d $102.82, ~48.8M shares, market cap ~$4.01B. (d) CONFIRMED against FDA: approval date, PDUFA date, full-vs-accelerated status, indication wording, and the stomatitis rates (72% with Grade 3 in 22% on the triplet; 58% with Grade 3 in 12% on the doublet).
evidence: FDA, 'FDA approves gedatolisib with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, for HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer', approval dated 14 July 2026 (against the 17 July 2026 PDUFA goal date set at the 20 January 2026 Priority Review acceptance): FULL approval in adults with HR+/HER2-, PIK3CA-wild-type locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after progression on endocrine therapy; VIKTORIA-1 PFS 9.3mo triplet (HR 0.24) and 7.4mo doublet (HR 0.33) vs 2.0mo fulvestrant; stomatitis 72% including Grade 3 in 22% (triplet) and 58% including Grade 3 in 12% (doublet), with mitigation generally effective and most patients resolving to a lower grade within 2 weeks. https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-gedatolisib-fulvestrant-or-without-palbociclib-hr-positive-her2-negative-locally -- CONFIRMS the catalyst fired favourably on a primary source, and is therefore spent.
